quirks: Statewide birth and death registration in Michigan began 1867, general compliance not reached until 1915 (FamilySearch Michigan Vital Records) - Mogan children born before ~1900 may lack filed birth records.

Detroit birth records since 1893 are obtained from the Wayne County Clerk; FamilySearch's unindexed Wayne County birth/death microfilm (1867-1917) explicitly excludes City of Detroit events, so Detroit births/deaths must be sought separately from county-wide ones.
Wayne County death index 1934-1953 held at Burton Historical Collection also excludes City of Detroit deaths; a separate Detroit Death Index (microfiche, 1920-current) covers Detroit proper.

A large number of Roman Catholic church records from the Archdiocese of Detroit (1704-1930, baptisms, marriages, deaths, first communions, confirmations) are on microfilm at the Burton Historical Collection, Detroit Public Library - the specific parish Mary McAndrew and John Mogan attended is not established by any tool result in this survey; search broadly across Detroit's Catholic parish registers.
Detroit streets were renumbered 1 January 1921 (same house, different numbers) - affects matching addresses across census years.

volume_search found 644 digitized volumes for Detroit 1870-1930; most Vital/Death group volumes (140 of 154) are browse-only images with no name index, and most Census volumes (55 of 69) are likewise browse-only despite being ~97-100% recordSearchablePercent on some specific rolls - check each volume's own searchability rather than assuming.
entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan (1870-1930)

## Jurisdiction overview
- Wayne County organized November 21, 1815; county seat Detroit, the oldest county in Michigan.
- Population (Wayne County): 1870: 119,068; 1880: 168,444; 1890: 257,114; 1900: 348,793; 1910: 531,591; 1920: 1,177,645; 1930: 1,888,946 (FamilySearch Wayne County Genealogy page).
- Large Irish Catholic immigrant population in Detroit in this era; parish-based Catholic recordkeeping common.
- No known courthouse record-loss disasters in Wayne County (per the wiki page).

## Boundary changes
Wayne County boundaries were established in 1815 as an original county and were stable through the 1870-1930 period; Detroit itself annexed surrounding land 1806-1926 (especially 1915-1925), which can change which jurisdiction a given Detroit address fell under historically, and streets were renumbered in 1921.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- Start date: statewide registration of births and deaths began in Michigan in 1867; general compliance by 1915 (FamilySearch Michigan Vital Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Michigan_Vital_Records). Marriage registration with the county clerk dates to 1805/county formation.
- What exists: FamilySearch "Michigan, Births, 1867-1902" and "Michigan, County Births, 1867-1917" (index & images); "Michigan, Deaths, 1867-1897" and "Michigan, Deaths and Burials, 1800-1995"; "Michigan, Death Certificates, 1921-1952."
- Where held: county level at the Wayne County Clerk for events in Wayne County generally; Detroit-specific births since 1893 come from the Wayne County Clerk, and Detroit deaths since 1897 from the Detroit Health Department. The FamilySearch Library's unindexed Wayne County birth/death microfilm (1867-1917) explicitly excludes City of Detroit events.
- Gaps: pre-1915 compliance was incomplete; Detroit deaths before 1897 are not separately described by a tool result.
- Pre-registration alternatives: church (Catholic parish) baptism/death records; obituaries; probate.

### Church records
- Denominations present: Catholic (large Irish and other immigrant population), Lutheran, LDS branches, others.

Irish Catholic family; baptisms stand in for missing civil births. Michigan, Church Records, 1819-1991 (2787825) is name-searchable; search parents' names. Tree holds Anna Irene christened 27 May 1885 (Wayne, Michigan). loc_001 says the family's parish is not established and Archdiocese of Detroit registers (1704-1930) are on microfilm at the Burton Historical Collection; the parish named in Anna Irene's christening, once read, should be the first register browsed there. Search Wayne County marriage returns (indexed marriage collections) and Catholic marriage entries to fix the earliest possible birth date; if the marriage was after 1876 only, no earlier child; a marriage before 1876 opens a window for children born 1870-1876. Check surname variants. The record may also name witnesses, relatives to follow.

STATE OF MICHIGAN

THE PROBATE COURT FOR THE COUNTY OF WAYNE

IN THE MATTER OF THE ESTATE OF $\text{Leopold Schultz}$
$\text{Deceased}$
To $\text{William Westphal and H J. Burghardt -}$
GREETING:

Having been appointed commissioners with full power and authority to receive, examine and adjust all claims and demands against said deceased, you will first be sworn to the faithful performance of your duties and, within thirty days from the date hereof, appoint convenient times and places, when and where you will meet for the purpose of examining and allowing such claims, and give notice thereof, and of the time hereby limited for creditors to present their claims, by personal service of such notice upon $\text{Herman Schultz, Admr wwa, of said estate}$
and by posting notices thereof in three public places in the $\text{City}$
of $\text{Detroit}$ in said county, and also by publishing such notice at least three weeks successively in the $\text{Detroit Legal News}$
a newspaper printed in said county. Either of you are authorized to administer oaths to parties and witnesses, when the same shall be required or proper for the investigation and trial of questions before you. Six months from this date were allowed by said court to the creditors of said deceased to present their claims to you for examination and allowance, at the expiration of which time, or as soon thereafter as you shall be able to complete the hearing of the claims presented, you are to made a report to said court of your proceedings in the examination and adjustment of said claims, embracing a list of the claims presented or exhibited in offset, and stating how much thereof was allowed and how much disallowed, together with the final balance in favor of the claimant or of said estate, as the case may be, which shall include interest to the date of your report. You are to note in distinct classes the claims allowed by you, in the following order: 1st. The necessary funeral expenses; 2nd. The expenses of the last sickness of said deceased; 3rd. Debts having a preference by the laws of the United States; 4th. Debts due other creditors. You will make due proof of the manner of giving said notice and return this commission with your report.

IN TESTIMONY WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand and affixed the seal of said court, at the city of Detroit, in said county, this $\text{thirteenth}$ day of $\text{February,}$
A. D. 190$\text{6.}$
$\text{Edgar O. Durfee}$
Judge of Probate.

$\left.\begin{array}{c}\text{STATE OF MICHIGAN} \\ \text{COUNTY OF WAYNE}\end{array}\right\}\text{ss.}$

On this $\text{21st}$ day of $\text{Febuary}$ A. D. 190$\text{6}$
before me personally appeared $\text{William Westphal and H. J.}$
$\text{Burghardt}$
the commissioners above named, and made oath that they would faithfully and impartially discharge the trust reposed in them by the foregoing commission as required by law. My commission expires
$\text{April 10th 1909}$
$\text{Sherman Littlefield}$
Notary Public, Wayne County, Mich.

COMMISSIONER ON CLAIMS' WARRANT. 4210 2-04

# State of Michigan,

## The Probate Court for the County of Wayne.

In the Matter of the Estate of Mary J. Wilcox —
Deceased.

To William Phillips and Eli K. Simonds —
Greeting:

Having been appointed commissioners, with full power and authority to receive, examine and adjust all claims and demands against said deceased, you will first be sworn to the faithful performance of your duties and, within thirty days from the date hereof, appoint convenient times and places, when and where you will meet for the purpose of examining and allowing such claims, and give notice thereof, and of the time hereby limited for creditors to present their claims, by personal service of such notice upon Josephus M. Burgess, Executor
and by posting notices thereof in three public places in the Village
of Northville in said county, and also by publishing such notice at least three weeks successively in the Northville Record
a newspaper printed in said county. Either of you are authorized to administer oaths to parties and witnesses, when the same shall be required or proper for the investigation and trial of questions before you. Six months from this date were allowed by said court to the creditors of said deceased to present their claims to you for examination and allowance, at the expiration of which time, or as soon thereafter as you shall be able to complete the hearing of the claims presented, you are to make a report to said court of your proceedings in the examination and adjustment of said claims, embracing a list of the claims presented or exhibited in offset, and stating how much thereof was allowed and how much disallowed, together with the final balance in favor of the claimant or of said estate, as the case may be, which shall include interest to the date of your report. You are to note in distinct classes the claims allowed by you, in the following order: 1st. The necessary funeral expenses; 2d. The expenses of the last sickness of said deceased; 3d. Debts having a preference by the laws of the United States; 4th. Debts due other creditors. You will make due proof of the manner of giving said notice and return this commission with your report.

In testimony whereof, I have hereunto set my hand and affixed the seal of said court, at the City of Detroit, in said county, this eleventh day of May —
A. D. 190 5.

Morse Rohnert
Circuit Judge for said county acting Judge of Probate.

    AT A SESSION OF SAID COURT, held at the Court house in the
City of Detroit, in said County, on the 31 day of Aug.,
in the year one thousand nine hundred and nine.
    Present, The Honorable: Joseph W. Donovan, Circuit Judge.
    It appearing to the satisfaction of the Court that the judg-
ment for Fifteen Hundred ($1500.00) Dollars, rendered by this
Court on the 7th day of October, A.D. 1908, in this cause, against
the above estate and in favor of Adam Krzywdzinski, appellant, was
not regular, in that, the appellee nor any of his representatives
were present when the same was rendered and had no notice of the
same for several months thereafter, that the proofs in said cause
were never closed, as should have been done before the entry of
judgment.
    Therefore, in the interest of justice, it is ordered that
said judgment be and the same is hereby vacated, and a new trial
of said cause granted, and that said cause be placed upon the
Docket of the September Term of this Court.
    It is further ordered that the appeal in this cause be and
the same is hereby reinstated.

                                        J W Donovan
                                        Circuit Judge.
